title: Divergence Timing and Cumulative Disagreement under KV-Cache Eviction
summary: This paper does not propose a replacement technique; it provides a measurement framework (coupling-based decomposition and residual-branch conditional Monte Carlo) that quantifies how KV-cache eviction policies such as SnapKV and recent-token retention diverge from full-cache generation. Adopting the analysis itself costs nothing at inference but requires instrumented paired trajectories to estimate divergence timing and exposure, which adds engineering complexity without changing serving performance. What can fail is transferability: the finding that 85-90% of mismatch mass comes from post-divergence exposure is an exploratory result on 288 documents and two 7-8B models, so eviction-policy rankings and window conclusions may not hold for other workloads, models, or retention budgets.
rationale: The paper is a diagnostic study rather than an adoptable method, and its comparative evidence on SnapKV retention settings is exploratory and confined to two open models, so it informs but does not yet justify changing a production eviction policy.
technique: Divergence analysis of KV-cache eviction policies
